name: Split Waggle Left
purpose: Waggle Right to the other edge, and the harder of the two. The quarterback's first steps are Dive Right's, the back away from the roll sells that dive, and he keeps going the way the dive's own fake takes him — out onto the left edge with our end in the flat in front of him. The split man is on the wrong end of the formation here, so instead of clearing that edge he runs deep from the back side. Run first, throw second.

RTE.rule: Engage the end over you for a count, then release and get across the field to eight yards. You are the second look and you arrive late on purpose.

LTE.rule: Engage the end over you for a count, then release to the flat at four yards and stay in front of the quarterback. You are the easy throw.

Z.rule: Sprint deep from the back side and lean toward the middle of the field. Nobody is throwing you the ball — you are holding their deep men away from the boot.

QB.rule: Fake the dive to the back away from your roll, hide the ball on your back hip, and get to the edge. Run it if it is open. Only throw if a defender comes up to take you.

LH.note: You are already on the side he rolls to — do not chase the fake.

RH.rule: Run the dive path full speed with your arms tucked like you have it. Their linebackers only leave if you are worth watching.

coaching_points: One pass in this formation is the right number. This is a running offence and the pass exists so the defence cannot put nine men in the box and forget about the edge.
Both ends must engage before releasing. If they run straight into their routes the fake dies.
The dive fake is the whole play. If that back does not get hit by somebody, he did not sell it.

The dive comes from the back away from the roll. The back on the side he rolls to never chases it — he stays home and protects that edge. Get those two backwards and the quarterback runs into his own blocker.

The Z is on the wrong end of the formation for this one, so he cannot clear the edge the quarterback is rolling to. He runs deep from the back side instead and holds their deep men there, which is what keeps the crosser open.
No blitzing is allowed for 8- and 9-year-olds, so the quarterback has time. Teach him to be patient and look up.
Run first, throw second. One throw, then tuck it — no scrambling backwards, ever.
